summary: Specifies an RTP payload format for the Variable-Rate Multimode Wideband (VMR-WB) speech codec and registers a media type for it. The format is designed to interoperate with existing VMR-WB transport formats on non-IP networks. It is standards-track and was updated by RFC 4424.

eli5.summary: A voice codec squeezes speech into small pieces. This explains how to pack those pieces into internet packets so they can be sent live and unpacked at the other end.

questions: how is vmr-wb carried over rtp
what is the vmr-wb header-free payload format
what is the cmr field in rtp audio
subtitle: How to pack VMR-WB wideband speech frames into RTP packets, including a header-free mode and a gateway-friendly octet-aligned mode.

tldr.problem: VMR-WB is a variable-rate wideband speech codec from 3GPP2 that is used on CDMA networks, and it needs a standard way to travel over IP in real time while still interoperating with existing non-IP formats and with AMR-WB.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two RTP payload formats, a header-free one holding a single frame and an octet-aligned one with a mode-request header, a table of contents and optional interleaving, plus a media type and SDP parameters.
tldr.outcome: Gateways can pass VMR-WB and AMR-WB speech without transcoding in the interoperable mode. It is a Proposed Standard that was updated by RFC 4424.

today: RFC 4348 is a Proposed Standard from January 2006 and is updated by RFC 4424. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: Scope of the Payload Format
sections.content:
RFC 4348 specifies how to packetize VMR-WB encoded speech into the Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP, see RFC 3550). The formats support single and multiple channels, frame interleaving, several frames per payload, a header-free payload, mode switching, and interoperation with existing VMR-WB transport formats on non-IP networks. A media type registration is included.

Because VMR-WB is interoperable with AMR-WB at certain rates, the document keeps as close as it can to RFC 3267 while optimizing for the modes that are not interoperable.
sections.eli5: This explains how to put squeezed voice sound into internet packets, using almost the same envelope as a similar codec called AMR-WB.

sections.title: The VMR-WB Codec and Its Modes
sections.content:
VMR-WB is the wideband speech standard developed by 3GPP2 for 3G CDMA cellular systems. It is a source-controlled, variable-rate, multimode codec: each operating mode trades voice quality against average data rate, and the mode is chosen from network traffic conditions and the desired quality of service. Frames use the CDMA2000 rates: full-rate 266 bits (13.3 kbps), half-rate 124 bits (6.2 kbps), quarter-rate 54 bits (2.7 kbps) and eighth-rate 20 bits (1.0 kbps).

Modes 0, 1 and 2 are the non-interoperable modes, and the encoder can switch among them without the decoder knowing in advance. Mode 3 is the interoperable mode, which matches AMR-WB codec modes 0, 1 and 2 at 6.60, 8.85 and 12.65 kbps. In mode 3 the encoder cannot switch between VMR-WB modes.

The codec can take 16000-Hz or 8000-Hz input, and the decoder outputs 16000 Hz by default. The RTP clock rate MUST always be 16000 Hz. The codec normally sends continuously, but it can use discontinuous transmission (DTX) over IP, sending silence descriptor frames during silence. Multi-channel audio is carried by encoding each channel separately and grouping the frames for the same 20 ms into a frame-block.
sections.eli5: The codec is like a note-taker who writes more detail when the speaker says something tricky and less when it is easy. It can also write in a style that another note-taker, AMR-WB, can read directly.

sections.title: Surviving Packet Loss
sections.content:
The octet-aligned format has two tools against lost packets. The first is redundant transmission: each packet repeats earlier frame-blocks along with the new ones, using a sliding window. The sender can use this without telling the receiver, because a packet with repeats looks like any other. If several versions of a frame arrive, the highest rate is RECOMMENDED. The sender should pick the amount of redundancy from feedback such as RTCP reports, and SHOULD NOT base it on the CMR. The RFC notes that RFC 2198 has lower overhead only when the time spread between primary and redundant data exceeds 5 frame times.

The second is interleaving. Putting several frame-blocks in one packet cuts overhead but a lost packet then loses consecutive frames, which sounds bad. Interleaving spreads the loss into single frame-block losses, at the cost of extra delay and receiver buffering. The receiver must signal support out of band, and streaming applications are the likely users.
sections.eli5: Sending the same sentence twice in two letters helps if one letter is lost. Mixing up the order of the words across letters means a lost letter only loses a few scattered words, not a whole sentence.

sections.title: Where VMR-WB Over IP Is Used
sections.content:
The RFC describes four scenarios. In the primary one, two IP terminals exchange VMR-WB over RTP, UDP and IP. Conversational use wants low delay and few frame-blocks per packet. Streaming can pack more per packet but is more exposed to loss.

In the second, a gateway connects a 3GPP2/CDMA2000 network to an IP terminal. The gateway forwards the codec mode request (CMR) in both directions, the IP terminal SHOULD follow it and SHOULD NOT set it. The third has gateways on both sides of the IP network between VMR-WB and AMR-WB mobile stations, where only VMR-WB mode 3 is used and the gateway forwards the minimum of three CMR values: from the IP side, its congestion choice, and its estimate of reception quality on the non-IP side. The fourth links two CDMA2000 networks that both use VMR-WB.
sections.eli5: Sometimes two internet phones talk directly, and sometimes a translator at the edge of a mobile network passes messages along. The translator also passes along requests like please talk a bit slower.

sections.title: RTP Header Use and the Header-Free Format
sections.content:
The RTP timestamp is the sampling instant of the first sample of the first frame-block, in units of samples at 16 kHz. One frame-block lasts 20 ms, which is 320 samples, so the timestamp rises by 320 per frame-block, even for 8 kHz media. The marker bit is always 0 in continuous transmission. In DTX it is 1 when the first frame-block of the packet holds the first speech frame of a talkspurt. The payload type is left to the RTP profile or dynamic binding.

The header-free format is for maximum efficiency, simplicity and minimum delay. Each packet holds exactly one speech frame with no payload header or table of contents, and the frame length tells the receiver the encoding rate. Because it is not compatible with the AMR-WB payload, only non-interoperable modes may be used, so FT=0, 1, 2 and 9 SHALL NOT appear. Interleaving is only available in the octet-aligned format. The default encoder mode is mode 0.
sections.eli5: The simplest envelope holds exactly one piece of voice and nothing else, so it is small and quick to open.

sections.title: The Octet-Aligned Payload
sections.content:
This payload has a payload header, a table of contents (ToC) and the speech data. Every field is padded with zero bits to an octet boundary. In the interoperable mode it is identical to the AMR-WB format of RFC 3267.

The header is 4 bits of CMR, 4 reserved bits that MUST be zero, and, only when interleaving is signaled, an 8-bit part with ILL and ILP, 4 bits each. CMR 0 to 2 request mode 3 at 6.60, 8.85 or 12.65 kbps, 3 asks for mode 2, 4 for mode 1, 5 for mode 0, 6 for mode 2 with maximum half-rate, and 15 means no preference. A request stays valid until a new one replaces it, and an invalid CMR MUST be ignored. Packets to a multicast group MUST carry CMR 15.

With interleaving, ILL=L means an interleave length of L+1 frame-blocks and ILP is the packet's index within the group, between 0 and ILL. The receiver sets the group-size limit with the interleaving parameter and the sender must keep N*(L+1) within it.

Each ToC entry is one octet describing one frame: F says whether another frame follows, FT is the frame type, and Q marks quality (0 means corrupted). Frame types 14 and 15 mean erasure and blank, and have no speech bits. A multi-channel packet with N channels and K frame-blocks has N*K entries, and speech frames follow in ToC order. An invalid FT means the payload MUST be discarded.
sections.eli5: The envelope has a front label with a request about how to speak next, a list saying what each piece of voice is, and then the pieces themselves in the same order as the list.

sections.title: Media Type Parameters and SDP
sections.content:
The RFC registers the media type audio/VMR-WB with the IETF tree and defines optional parameters. mode-set restricts which modes (0 to 3) the encoder may use. channels defaults to 1. octet-align set to 1 selects the octet-aligned format, while 0 or absent means header-free. interleaving gives the maximum interleave group size and requires octet-align. dtx set to 1 allows silence descriptor frames, and ptime and maxptime are also used.

In SDP the clock rate in a=rtpmap MUST be 16000, and other parameters go in a=fmtp. In offer and answer, rate, channel and payload settings are used symmetrically, mode-set is declarative and only modes both ends support are used. A VMR-WB terminal SHOULD also declare AMR-WB with modes 0, 1 and 2 and octet-align so that interoperable connections are possible.

Implementations SHALL support both header-free and octet-aligned formats. Interleaving is optional.
sections.eli5: Before talking, the two sides agree on settings, like which envelope to use and how fast to talk. These settings are written in a small note that both can read.

sections.title: Congestion Control and Security
sections.content:
General RTP congestion control applies (RFC 3550 and RFC 3551), and it is required for any transmission over unmanaged best-effort networks. The IP sender manages congestion using feedback such as RTCP, and can change the operating mode, the redundancy, or the number of frames per packet. Redundancy itself must be regulated so that it does not cause congestion.

The payload format has no built-in security, so external mechanisms such as SRTP MAY be used. All audio data bits MUST be encrypted for confidentiality. Interleaving can weaken a key change for a short time, since frames sent earlier under the old key can still be concealed into intelligible audio. A man in the middle can replace audio or tamper with the CMR to lower quality, so an external authentication mechanism MUST be used. The RFC sees little risk of denial of service from malformed data.
sections.eli5: Do not flood the road with too many cars. The envelope has no lock, so use a locked mailbag if the message is private.
